comment: Configuration for the repository's agent work-tracking workflow (GitHub Issues + GitHub Projects), introduced by issue #177.

Skills under .agents/skills/ (canonical location; .claude/skills/<name> are relative symlinks to ../../.agents/skills/<name> for Claude Code) reference this file instead of hardcoding project or field identifiers.
Opaque identifiers (project item/field/status IDs, view IDs) are never stored here or in skills; agents resolve them at runtime with `gh` from the names below.

issueTracker.role: canonical record for work scope, design proposals and decisions, acceptance criteria, implementation plans, verification evidence, blockers, and handoffs

defaultProject.name: Pohunek
defaultProject.role: default delivery tracking for actionable repository work

authorization.standing: The repository owner durably pre-authorizes agents to create issues, edit their own body sections, comment, add native sub-issue/dependency links on the repository above, and add items to / set status in the default project, without asking first. This overrides any generic 'confirm outward-facing actions' default.
authorization.neverAsk: Never ask whether to file an issue or offer a follow-up instead of filing it; verified out-of-scope findings and verified defects noticed incidentally are filed automatically after dedup.
authorization.askOnly: Ask only which issue applies when competing matches or a genuinely ambiguous scope make that unclear.
authorization.notCovered: Commits, pushes, issue closure outside the Done bar, and destructive project edits still follow their own rules.

pullRequests.policy: Deliver work as a stack of small, sequential PRs, each one coherent concern, landed bottom-up. A single PR is right only when the whole change is already one small concern.
pullRequests.sliceRules: Every PR is complete production code for its slice: it builds, passes the applicable full gate set on its own, carries the test scenarios its change needs under the Testing policy in .agents/instructions/verification.md (integration scenarios driving cooperating production components through a supported boundary, or E2E scenarios driving the real product processes — never a new unit test, no coverage targets), and updates docs/knowledge/ and docs/public-api.md for any surface it touches. No stubs, dead code, or placeholders a later PR fills in. Slices follow dependency order; the stack as a whole delivers the full DoD.
pullRequests.softMaxNote: Hand-written changed lines per PR, excluding tests, lockfiles, and generated files. A cue to split, not a hard limit: a coherent slice beats an arbitrary cut.
pullRequests.issueReferences: Non-final PRs use 'Refs #N'; only the final PR of the stack uses 'Closes #N'.
pullRequests.retargetNote: The repository does not delete head branches on merge, so GitHub never auto-retargets the next stacked PR: retarget it to the default branch explicitly after the PR below it merges.

statusSemantics.Todo: Tracked, actionable work that has not started yet. For a design-proposal issue, Todo means only that it is tracked pending a decision — it does not imply the proposed design is accepted; acceptance is an explicit decision recorded on the issue.
statusSemantics.In Progress: Work is being implemented, reviewed, or awaiting verification. Represent review findings and blockers as issue comments while status stays In Progress; do not invent a Review or Blocked status.
statusSemantics.Done: The issue is closed as completed: for any repository change (code, scripts, harness files, docs, skills, configuration), verified landing on the remote default branch with all DoD items met; only pure planning/investigation with no repository change may complete on the issue-held artifact/evidence. Never set Done when only opening a PR or merging locally without an authorized remote push.

issueClosure.order: DoD verified -> close issue as completed -> sync Project status Done.
issueClosure.landing: A repository change of any kind (code, scripts, docs, skills, config) needs a verified remote default-branch landing before the issue may close; local merge without an authorized push stays In Progress with local-merge evidence.
issueClosure.noDodShuffling: Unmet original DoD items are never moved to follow-up issues to claim the current issue done; verified out-of-scope findings may be filed as separate follow-up issues.

additionalProjects.role: Existing topic projects remain additional views. No destructive migrations; do not remove items from them. List them with `gh` and update only when the task explicitly covers a topic view.

issueBodyRoles.body: Full scope, accepted decisions with their rationale, definition-of-done items with stable IDs (D1, D2, ...), dependencies, and the plan. Long-lived content; prefer editing own sections over rewriting.
issueBodyRoles.comments: Progress reports, verification evidence (commands run and results), handoffs, blockers, and status-change rationale. Append, never overwrite others' comments.

meaning.ready: Public eligibility only: objective scope, stable D1..Dn, exact focused checks, capability and size, prerequisites, resolved dependencies, and a named available review route are recorded; no active recognized assignment or linked active PR makes immediate work misleading. It is not a reservation, vacancy proof, grant, merge promise, or private Project status.
meaning.design-needed: A decision, scope, acceptance criterion, or review route needed before implementation remains unresolved.
meaning.blocked: A named dependency or external prerequisite prevents eligible work from starting.

readiness.manualProjection: Readiness labels are manual public projections, never reservations or locks; contributionPolicy.reservations defines how a reservation is granted.

capabilities.docs: Documentation, knowledge sources, and user-facing written contracts.
capabilities.rust: Rust crates, binaries, and core behavior.
capabilities.typescript-sdk: The TypeScript SDK workspace and its release artifacts.
capabilities.platform-native: Operating-system integrations, native supervision, and platform-specific behavior.
capabilities.github-workflow: Issue/PR forms, repository workflow configuration, and agent guidance.
capabilities.verification: Test, gate, compatibility, or evidence work that does not primarily change another capability area.

meaning.S: One bounded change with a focused verification path.
meaning.M: Several related changes or multiple affected components with a clear verification path.
meaning.L: Broad or cross-cutting work that should normally be split into sequential, independently verifiable slices.

size.note: A scope cue only; never a promised time budget.

publicContribution.deliveryStatus: Todo, In Progress, and Done retain the meanings in statusSemantics; readiness is separate. A public contributor does not need private Project access.
publicContribution.review: The review route and integration authority are defined by contributionPolicy.reviewAndIntegration.

localFiles.NEXT.md: Not a work authority and never required by any workflow. A pre-existing untracked NEXT.md is a migration read-only source at most.
localFiles.SiYuan: Optional personal notes/pointers; never a competing project authority.

contributionPolicy.accountability: The authenticated GitHub principal is accountable; agent and run identifiers are correlation metadata only. Public issue, dependency, reservation, and pull request evidence must be sufficient without private Project access.

may: submit pull requests and evidence, including unsolicited pull requests
outsideContributor.limits: No repository write, private Project, host, credential, model budget, review, merge, release, or privileged-label authority is conferred. The repository owner's standing agent authorization does not transfer.

reservations.beforeService: A maintainer explicitly records and reconciles a manual reservation after checking active work, the principal's outstanding reservations, comments, and pull requests; record it in public issue evidence. A request, label, assignee, or unanswered comment is not a grant; a manual record is not an atomic lease.
reservations.afterService: Automatic admission is unavailable until #805–#811 deliver a coordination service that authenticates principals and transactionally enforces published eligibility, capacity, WIP, expiry, anti-hoarding, and assignment transitions. Its per-principal and repository limits cannot be reset by changing an agent or run identifier. GitHub labels, assignees, and Project fields are projections, never locks, and the service grants no general merge or release authority. Numeric limits belong to #805 and are not set here.
reservations.custody: A recognized holder acts only within granted scope and the current authenticated generation; once the service exists it may renew, submit, release, or request transfer. It cannot expand scope, transfer ownership unilaterally, release a successor's assignment, or count submission as acceptance. Submission and review retain custody. Expiry or abandonment starts reconciliation of linked pull requests, branches, candidate evidence, and pending effects before an explicit release, adoption, cancellation, or transfer; it never silently frees or reassigns the work. A stale holder cannot mutate a successor assignment.
reservations.handoff: A custody handoff preserves the holder, generation when available, issue/spec revision, exact commit or pull request, actual checks, unresolved effects, and the next permitted action. Acknowledging a handoff does not transfer custody.

reviewAndIntegration.maintainer: zajca triages, routes, resolves disputes, and integrates contributions after the required gates and independent review under existing authorization. Product or authority changes require the applicable owner decision.
reviewAndIntegration.reviewer: An available independent reviewer examines the relevant code, contract, and evidence for the area, assesses the exact candidate against the issue criteria, and records findings without needing an implementation reservation. No permanently staffed area reviewer or response-time commitment is claimed. The submitter, author, executor, and manager cannot supply independent approval, including through another session used to author or direct the change; a fresh review-only session that did not author the change supplies the technical review (the marker). Starting that session with a review-only briefing is not directing the change.
reviewAndIntegration.unavailable: If no independent reviewer is available, the candidate remains unaccepted; the maintainer records the state and retries routing when capacity exists.
reviewAndIntegration.automatedReview: The technical review gate is an opus-pr-review:v1 marker comment authored by zajca that names the exact pull request head, posted by an Opus (high effort) review session. GO is high=0 and medium=0; a review with only LOW findings passes and each LOW finding becomes a follow-up issue. A marker from any other author, for another head, or from an interrupted run is not approval. No label is needed. On an outside contribution the marker is the technical gate only: the merge also needs the maintainer's explicit approval.
reviewAndIntegration.reviewBroker: No broker and no label request the review. For each head the maintainer approves the workflow runs, then the maintainer's manager requests the Opus review; if no marker has arrived some hours after green CI, the contributor mentions the maintainer on the pull request. An outside contributor never receives the credential that posts the marker and cannot supply it; only the designated independent review session (a fresh Opus high effort session that did not author the change, started by the maintainer's manager, the coordinator or operator, or by the delivering agent when no manager is named) posts the marker, and the authoring agent never posts or imitates one.
reviewAndIntegration.forkHeads: A fork head is never dispatched, run through a ref such as refs/pull/<N>/head, or have its jobs rerun by an agent in this repository. For an outside pull request the maintainer reviews the full diff, workflow files included, then re-creates the change on a maintainer branch and dispatches that branch, or relies on the post-merge main run. Fork-provided workflow YAML runs only in the approved, read-only pull_request run.
reviewAndIntegration.authority: Review does not grant merge authority. Outside contributors receive no merge or release authority. Release remains separately authorized.

competingWorkAndAppeals.unsolicitedPullRequests: Remain welcome without a recognized reservation and are evaluated against the same criteria. A reservation neither guarantees a merge nor prevents competing fork work. Selecting a different candidate requires an explicit integration and custody decision.
competingWorkAndAppeals.conflicts: Disclose conflicts. Author, executor, and manager cannot replace independent acceptance by using another session they used to author or direct the change; a fresh review-only session that did not author the change can supply the technical review.
competingWorkAndAppeals.appeals: Cite the contested decision, policy/spec revision, and new evidence on the issue or pull request through the maintainer route. An appeal or handoff acknowledgment does not itself change custody, transfer the work, or grant acceptance.

contributionPolicy.enforcement: This is accepted workflow guidance, not a runtime permission grant. Normal GitHub controls remain in force; automatic reservation enforcement does not exist before the coordination service is delivered.
contributionPolicy.ownerAgent: The owner agent retains only existing standing issue and Project authorization and separately authorized task scope; recognized assignments, reservation scope, and conflicts remain binding on it. Commits, pushes, and releases require their own authorization; none is granted to outside contributors.
